paragraphs: Training several neural networks on overlapping datasets can repeat the same expensive preparation work. Each job separately reads and preprocesses examples, even when another job has already prepared them. A shared cache helps only if jobs request reusable data before it is displaced. Independent random sampling makes that coordination difficult and can cause frequent cache replacement.

The paper introduces a dependent sampling algorithm and a cache policy designed for this setting. A new tree structure makes the sampling algorithm efficient to implement. Together, these components underpin Joader, a prototype dataloader that shares preparation work across jobs whose datasets overlap only partially. The approach relaxes earlier requirements that all jobs use identical datasets and request examples in synchronized order.

Evaluations in practical training scenarios report greater versatility and training speed improvements reaching 500% for ResNet18. This is a reported maximum, rather than a uniform improvement across workloads. The contribution addresses the data supply side of training: coordinating access can reduce duplicated preparation and improve training speed.
neurips-2022-a-deep-learning-dataloader-.tldr: Joader coordinates sampling and caching so parallel training jobs can share data preparation even when their datasets overlap only partially.

paragraphs: Changing how many examples an algorithm processes together can change its learning behavior. The paper calls an algorithm batch size-invariant when adjustments to other hyperparameters can largely compensate for that change. Ordinary stochastic gradient descent has this property at small batch sizes through learning-rate adjustments, but some policy optimization algorithms, including PPO, do not.

The authors trace the difficulty to how these algorithms restrict policy updates. Their solution separates two reference policies with different jobs. The proximal policy controls the size of an update, while the behavior policy accounts for the policy that generated the training data through off-policy corrections. Decoupling these roles makes it possible to adjust batch size without tying both mechanisms to the same reference.

The paper shows how this modification makes the affected algorithms batch size-invariant in the stated sense. Experiments also help explain their behavior and demonstrate more efficient use of stale data. The practical significance is greater flexibility in training configuration and data reuse, with invariance meaning approximate compensation rather than identical behavior under every batch size.
neurips-2022-batch-size-invariance-for-p.tldr: Separating the policies used for update control and data correction makes policy optimization more adaptable to batch-size changes and stale data.

paragraphs: Generating high-resolution images with transformers can be slow and computationally complicated. CogView2 addresses this problem through a hierarchical transformer design and local parallel autoregressive generation. The approach combines a hierarchy for image generation with a mechanism for carrying out local generation work in parallel, targeting the difficulty of producing detailed images efficiently.

The system begins with CogLM, a transformer containing six billion parameters. It is pretrained using a self-supervised task that brings text and images into a cross-modal language-modeling framework. The authors then fine-tune this model for fast super-resolution, the stage concerned with increasing image resolution. This connects broad cross-modal pretraining with a more specialized image-generation capability.

The resulting system is reported to produce images that are highly competitive with the contemporary DALL-E-2 system. It also supports interactive editing in which text guides changes to an image. The stated contribution therefore combines an efficiency-oriented generation design with competitive image generation and a text-based editing capability, without claiming universal superiority over the comparison system.
neurips-2022-cogview2-faster-and-better-.tldr: CogView2 combines hierarchical transformers, local parallel generation, and super-resolution training for competitive text-to-image generation and interactive editing.

paragraphs: Principal component analysis represents data using directions derived from its covariance matrix. Those directions can be unstable when their associated eigenvalues are close together. This paper connects covariance-based analysis with graph neural networks, which learn from relationships between elements, and asks whether that connection can yield a more stable approach.

The proposed coVariance neural network, or VNN, treats a sample covariance matrix as a graph on which the network operates. The motivation comes from similarities between PCA's use of covariance eigenspaces and graph convolutional filters. The authors theoretically establish stability to perturbations in the covariance matrix, providing a basis for handling changes that can disrupt standard PCA-based analysis.

Experiments on real datasets support the stability result and show more stable performance than PCA-based statistical approaches. Experiments involving multiple resolutions also demonstrate transfer of performance across covariance matrices with different dimensions, a capability the abstract contrasts with PCA-based approaches. These findings support using covariance relationships as a learnable structure for stable analysis and transfer across resolutions.
neurips-2022-covariance-neural-networks-.tldr: VNNs treat covariance matrices as graphs, with theoretical stability guarantees and experimental evidence of stability and transfer across matrix dimensions.

paragraphs: A time-series classifier must decide how much of a signal to consider when recognizing a pattern. This span is its receptive field. Choosing an appropriate span is difficult because useful patterns can occur at different scales, both across examples and within one signal. A manually chosen receptive field can therefore be an awkward fit for varied data.

The paper proposes a dynamic sparse network that learns connections covering different receptive fields. Its layers use sparse kernels, and dynamic sparse training explores their connections within constrained regions. This makes the choice of what parts of the signal to use part of training, reducing the need for cumbersome receptive-field hyperparameter tuning while creating opportunities to reduce resource use.

Experiments report state-of-the-art classification performance on both single-variable and multiple-variable time-series datasets. The reported computational cost is less than half that of recent baseline methods. These results suggest that sparse, adaptable connections can support both accuracy and efficiency in the evaluated tasks, rather than requiring dense computation to capture patterns at multiple scales.
neurips-2022-dynamic-sparse-network-for-.tldr: A dynamic sparse network learns which signal spans to use, achieving reported state-of-the-art time-series classification with less than half the baseline computational cost.

paragraphs: A model can perform well on its evaluation data yet be sensitive to small changes in the data distribution. This paper develops a way to search proactively for plausible changes that cause large performance differences. It describes shifts through parameter changes in the causal mechanisms governing observed variables, with parameter constraints defining the distributions considered plausible.

The objective is to find the worst loss within this robustness set. Estimating each shifted loss by reweighting data is possible, but the search is non-convex and estimates can have high variance. For small shifts, the authors instead approximate the loss locally to second order. This turns the search into a particular quadratic optimization problem for which efficient algorithms exist.

For shifts in conditional exponential-family models, the paper shows how to estimate the approximation directly and bounds its error. An image-based gender classification application reveals sensitivity to changes in non-causal attributes. The result illustrates how a structured, local robustness analysis can expose vulnerabilities to specified distribution changes.
neurips-2022-evaluating-robustness-to-da.tldr: The paper searches for damaging small distribution shifts using constrained causal parameters and an efficiently optimized second-order loss approximation.

paragraphs: Understanding a visual scene requires grouping its elements and deciding what belongs to the foreground or background. This becomes difficult when their appearances are similar. The paper investigates whether configuration cues associated with human figure-ground perception can help convolutional networks resolve that ambiguity, beyond learning appearance features and hierarchical context.

The authors introduce a Figure-Ground-Aided module that learns statistics of scene configuration. They explicitly supervise it to recognize cues such as convexity and lower-region placement, which are relevant to human perceptual organization. An Interactive Enhancement Module then uses these learned configuration priors to assist representation learning, connecting the figure-ground cues to the network's visual features.

A dedicated visual segregation test evaluates the proposed mechanism directly. Broader evaluations report improvements across several baseline models, while a model augmented with the mechanism outperforms state-of-the-art approaches on four real-world applications. The findings support configuration-aware supervision as a useful way to improve perceptual organization in visually ambiguous scenes, with evidence spanning both a targeted test and application-level performance.
neurips-2022-exploring-figure-ground-ass.tldr: Explicitly teaching figure-ground configuration cues improves convolutional networks' perceptual organization in visually ambiguous scenes.

paragraphs: A latent-variable model can fit observed data without recovering the underlying factors that generated it. This is a central difficulty in nonlinear independent component analysis, where statistically independent hidden variables are transformed into observations by a deterministic nonlinear function. In unrestricted settings, multiple spurious explanations can match the data perfectly.

The paper studies whether restricting the mixing function can resolve this ambiguity. It focuses on constraints on the Jacobian, the matrix describing how each output changes with each input. Orthogonal coordinate transformations require the columns of this matrix to be mutually orthogonal. The authors examine these transformations and a more restricted subclass called conformal maps.

The strongest stated result is an identifiability proof for conformal maps. Additional theoretical results suggest that the broader orthogonal class has properties that prevent certain families of spurious solutions from undermining identifiability in generic settings. The distinction matters: the paper proves identifiability for the subclass while providing supporting theoretical evidence for the broader class. Its contribution clarifies how structural restrictions can help recover meaningful latent factors.
neurips-2022-function-classes-for-identi.tldr: The paper proves identifiability for conformal mixing functions and provides theoretical evidence that broader orthogonal transformations resist spurious nonlinear ICA solutions.

paragraphs: Understanding how variables behave together requires attention to both ordinary observations and rare extremes. Extreme observations are scarce, making their dependencies difficult to estimate. Archimax copulas provide a framework for modeling dependencies in the main body and tails of a distribution together, potentially allowing common observations to inform estimates of rare behavior.

The authors build on the stochastic representation of this distribution family to develop a non-parametric inference method and a sampling algorithm. These methods address both learning dependencies from data and generating observations from the resulting model. Their intended advantage is flexible, scalable use of Archimax copulas without treating the bulk and tails as disconnected modeling problems.

Comparisons with state-of-the-art density-modeling techniques suggest that the method extrapolates effectively into the tails while scaling to higher-dimensional data. The authors identify healthcare and safety as possible application areas where ordinary and extreme behavior need to be understood together. These are proposed uses; the stated experimental finding concerns tail extrapolation and scalability.
neurips-2022-inference-and-sampling-for-.tldr: New inference and sampling methods make Archimax copulas more practical for jointly modeling common observations and rare multivariate extremes.

paragraphs: A moving sound source produces audio that differs from a stationary one, particularly when moving toward or away from a microphone. This paper uses the connection between sound and motion for two linked tasks: separating sounds using video and predicting a sounding object's three-dimensional motion from its separated audio.

The Audio Separator and Motion Predictor framework represents the scene with a 2.5D graph. It combines depth predictions from individual video frames, aligns those predictions, and associates scene regions with detected objects. The resulting graph describes objects and their approximate spatial proximity. The model recursively divides this graph into subgraphs associated with individual sounds while jointly predicting source motion from the separated audio.

Experiments on Audio Separation in the Wild and Audio Visual Event report better sound separation than prior work on both datasets. The system also estimates source motion direction better than comparison methods. These findings support treating scene structure, source motion, and sound separation as connected learning problems, with the graph supplying spatial organization to the joint task.
neurips-2022-learning-audio-visual-dynam.tldr: ASMP jointly separates sounds and predicts source motion using a scene graph built from video objects and approximate depth.

paragraphs: Observations of a physical system may reveal its behavior without directly exposing states such as position and velocity or parameters such as friction and elasticity. This paper estimates both from observation sequences. Its setting assumes that a governing dynamic equation is supplied, while the physical parameters within that equation remain unknown.

The model couples an autoencoder with a parameter estimator. The autoencoder compresses measurements or images into a sequence of latent states, incorporating simulation of the supplied equation to make those states consistent with physics. The estimator predicts the unknown physical parameters. The authors also study Fourier feature mappings and provide theoretical and empirical evidence that these improve parameter-estimation generalization compared with using raw state sequences.

Experiments cover three visual tasks and one task using sensor measurements. The reported results show interpretable latent states and better generalization for long-term dynamics prediction than state-of-the-art baselines. The contribution is a way to combine known physical structure with learned states and parameters, so that prediction benefits from the supplied dynamics.
neurips-2022-learning-physics-constraine.tldr: A physics-constrained autoencoder jointly learns interpretable states and unknown physical parameters, improving long-term prediction in the evaluated tasks.

paragraphs: Predicting future facts about a newly appearing entity is difficult when a knowledge graph contains only a few observations about it. The available evidence may be too limited to train a model from scratch, and relationships can change between the initial observations and the future. The paper addresses these combined challenges of scarce supervision and temporal change.

MetaTKGR learns how to sample and aggregate neighboring information from recent facts. Instead of applying a fixed neighborhood rule, it adjusts these strategies using supervision from future facts as feedback during learning. This allows its representation of a new entity to account for evolving relationships. The framework also includes a temporal adaptation regularizer, supported by theoretical analysis, to stabilize reasoning over time.

Experiments on three real-world temporal knowledge graphs report a large improvement over eight state-of-the-art baselines. The findings support adapting the information-gathering process itself when reasoning about new entities. This matters because a representation useful immediately after an entity appears may need to change as its surrounding facts evolve.
neurips-2022-learning-to-sample-and-aggr.tldr: MetaTKGR adapts how it samples and combines recent graph facts to predict future relationships for entities with very few observations.

paragraphs: When a user moves a few handles on a three-dimensional object, a shape-editing system must determine how the rest of its surface should deform. Common approaches repeatedly optimize the mesh using manually designed deformation regularizers. This paper instead learns deformation behavior from shape geometry and a large dataset containing varied non-rigid deformations.

Given a source mesh and target handle positions, the method predicts a continuous deformation field throughout three-dimensional space. A transformer-based network represents the overall deformation by composing local surface deformations. It learns local latent codes anchored at positions in space, then uses those codes to define continuous deformation functions for the corresponding surface regions.

The authors evaluate the method on DeformingThing4D and compare it with both traditional optimization methods and recent neural approaches. They report that it handles challenging shape changes and generalizes well to unseen deformations. The contribution is a learned geometric prior that translates partial user instructions into broader surface changes through a spatially continuous representation.
neurips-2022-neural-shape-deformation-pr.tldr: A transformer learns local deformation functions that combine into continuous mesh edits guided by user-moved handles.

paragraphs: The ability to express a function with a neural network does not by itself establish that training can learn it efficiently. This paper proves limitations for networks trained with noisy gradient descent when the training procedure is equivariant. Equivariance means that relevant transformations produce corresponding transformations in training behavior, a property shared by many standard architectures and initializations.

One application characterizes which functions fully connected networks can weak-learn on the binary hypercube and the unit sphere. Within this task, the result shows that depth-two networks are as powerful as networks of any other depth. This is a statement about the specified learning setting, rather than a general claim that depth never helps neural networks.

The paper also extends a necessary structural condition for learning latent low-dimensional functions beyond the mean-field regime. Separately, it establishes hardness results for fully connected networks trained with stochastic gradient descent under cryptographic assumptions. Together, these results show how training symmetries and computational assumptions can constrain efficient learning, even when flexible neural architectures are available.
neurips-2022-on-the-non-universality-of-.tldr: The paper proves conditional limits on efficient neural-network learning arising from equivariant gradient training and, separately, cryptographic assumptions.

paragraphs: Learning to stabilize an unknown dynamical system requires gathering information while the system is already evolving. For linear time-invariant systems, the paper studies how many observations are needed along a single trajectory. Existing leading approaches require a number of samples linear in the state dimension, which the abstract associates with state magnitudes growing exponentially in that dimension.

The proposed algorithm uses spectral decomposition to focus learning on the unstable subspace. Instead of learning the entire dynamical matrix, it learns only the part acting on that subspace. This targets the components of the dynamics responsible for instability, making the amount of information required depend on the system's instability index as well as its overall dimension.

Under appropriate assumptions, the authors prove stabilization using O(k log n) samples, where n is the state dimension and k is the instability index. They present this as the first sublinear sample-complexity result in the stated low-instability regime. The guarantee is conditional, and its significance is that stabilization can require learning substantially less than the full system.
neurips-2022-on-the-sample-complexity-of.tldr: Under suitable assumptions, learning only unstable dynamics allows stabilization from a single trajectory using O(k log n) samples.

paragraphs: A recurrent neural network can have a large, complicated connectivity matrix, making it difficult to explain how its connections generate useful dynamics. Earlier theoretical understanding often relied on specially constrained connectivity. This paper examines networks trained without such constraints on several tasks previously used in neuroscience, asking which parts of their connectivity actually matter.

The authors identify operative dimensions: components of the connectivity whose removal strongly changes local network dynamics. These dimensions define a low-dimensional, functionally relevant subspace of the weight matrix. In the studied networks, rebuilding the matrix from only a few operative dimensions is sufficient to preserve the original task performance.

This finding indicates that much of the apparent high-dimensional connectivity is functionally unnecessary for those trained tasks. It also makes the relationship between connections and dynamics easier to study by reducing the relevant structure. The authors suggest that separate subspaces might host independent functions to help avoid catastrophic forgetting in continual learning; that possibility is a proposed implication, rather than a demonstrated continual-learning result.
neurips-2022-operative-dimensions-in-unc.tldr: A few functionally important connectivity dimensions preserve performance in the studied unconstrained RNNs, revealing a compact structure behind their dynamics.

paragraphs: Training adversarial models involves interacting players whose updates can destabilize one another. The paper introduces Level k Gradient Play to stabilize minimax learning through recursive reasoning about future strategies. The method uses gradients without requiring second-order information or the sophisticated heuristics associated with some predictive-update approaches.

As the reasoning level k increases, the authors show that the method approaches an accurate estimate of the players' future strategies. Its infinite-level form generalizes a family of provably convergent predictive game dynamics. The convergence results distinguish settings: local convergence is established for nonconvex-nonconcave zero-sum games, while global convergence is established for bilinear and quadratic games.

Combined with Adam, the method shows reported advantages in performance and computational overhead. For unconditional CIFAR-10 generation, the authors report an FID of 10.17 within 30 hours on one Nvidia RTX3090, using 30 times fewer parameters than BigGAN. This experiment supports the practicality of the approach on common computing resources, while the theoretical guarantees retain their stated game-specific scope.
neurips-2022-recursive-reasoning-in-mini.tldr: Level k Gradient Play recursively anticipates opponents' strategies, with setting-specific convergence guarantees and practical gains in GAN training.

paragraphs: An agent learning from images needs a representation of the scene that supports choosing useful actions. This paper investigates whether supervision from a neural radiance field can produce such a representation. Its central question is whether a visual representation trained this way is useful for downstream reinforcement learning in robotic manipulation.

NeRF-RL trains an encoder to map multiple image observations into a latent description of the scene's objects. A decoder built from a neural radiance field is conditioned on that latent description and supplies the supervision used to learn it. The reinforcement-learning algorithm then uses the learned latent space as its state representation, connecting image-based representation learning to action learning.

Experiments involve hanging mugs on hooks, pushing objects, and opening doors. The results indicate that NeRF supervision produces representations better suited to these tasks than other learned representations, and can even improve on low-dimensional hand-engineered state information. This is evidence that the way a representation is trained can matter as much as its compactness for the evaluated manipulation problems.
neurips-2022-reinforcement-learning-with.tldr: NeRF-RL uses neural radiance field supervision to learn image-based state representations that improve reinforcement learning in evaluated manipulation tasks.

paragraphs: Self-supervised learning on heterogeneous information networks often depends on carefully constructing positive and negative examples. Those design choices can make methods difficult to adapt and can affect their ability to generalize. This paper proposes SHGP, a pretraining approach that obtains supervision from structural clustering without generating either kind of example.

SHGP has two modules that use the same attention-based aggregation scheme. At each iteration, Att-LPA groups objects according to graph structure and produces pseudo-labels. Att-HGNN uses those labels to learn object representations and attention coefficients. The two modules reinforce one another, connecting the grouping of graph objects with the learning of representations that distinguish them.

Experiments on four real-world datasets report better effectiveness than state-of-the-art unsupervised baselines and even semi-supervised baselines. The results support structural clustering as a useful source of training signals for heterogeneous graphs. The methodological significance is that supervision can emerge from an iterative relationship between graph organization and representation learning, reducing dependence on customized positive and negative example construction.
neurips-2022-self-supervised-heterogeneo.tldr: SHGP pretrains heterogeneous graph representations through mutually reinforcing structural clustering and attention learning without positive or negative example generation.

paragraphs: Federated learning combines updates from multiple clients while leaving their data local. Many convergence analyses assume that noise in gradient information has finite variance. This paper addresses heavier-tailed noise that can violate that assumption, a situation reported in federated-learning research and one that falls outside many existing guarantees.

The proposed FAT-Clipping framework combines federated averaging, two-sided learning rates, and clipping. It has per-round and per-iteration variants, distinguished by how frequently clipping is performed. The analysis assumes a bounded alpha-moment for an alpha between one and two, allowing treatment of some noise distributions whose variance need not be finite. The authors derive rates for strongly convex and general nonconvex settings.

The per-iteration variant requires more clipping operations, but the paper establishes additional benefits: linear speedup with the number of local client updates and rates matching a lower bound in order. These results clarify a tradeoff between clipping effort and theoretical efficiency. The contribution extends convergence analysis beyond finite-variance noise while retaining an explicit moment condition on the noise.
neurips-2022-taming-fat-tailed-heavier-t.tldr: FAT-Clipping provides federated-learning convergence results under bounded-moment noise assumptions that can allow infinite variance, with extra efficiency guarantees for per-iteration clipping.

paragraphs: Many learning procedures need to know how an optimization solution changes when its inputs or parameters change. Unrolled differentiation estimates this sensitivity by running an iterative solver and differentiating through its sequence of computations. The paper studies how quickly the resulting Jacobian estimate converges, focusing on quadratic objectives solved by gradient descent or the Chebyshev method.

The analysis gives finite-iteration convergence rates and exposes a learning-rate tradeoff. A larger learning rate can produce fast asymptotic convergence of the Jacobian, but may come with an arbitrarily long initial burn-in phase. A smaller learning rate can provide immediate convergence, though at a slower rate. The authors call this tension the curse of unrolling.

The result matters because behavior after many iterations can conceal a long period before derivative estimates become useful. It provides a theoretical way to distinguish eventual convergence speed from progress early in the computation. The paper also identifies open questions, including a practical update rule for choosing an optimal unrolling strategy and connections to Sobolev orthogonal polynomials.
neurips-2022-the-curse-of-unrolling-rate.tldr: For quadratic optimization, unrolled differentiation faces a tradeoff between fast eventual Jacobian convergence with potentially long burn-in and slower immediate convergence.

paragraphs: Sign language conveys meaning through both manual articulation and non-manual elements. A model trained directly on color video must find these signals among substantial visual redundancy, which can cause it to overlook important information. The paper introduces an encoder that combines the original video with a more structured description of movement.

The encoder has two streams: one processes raw video, and the other processes keypoint sequences from an existing keypoint estimator. The authors explore ways to make the streams interact, including bidirectional connections, a sign pyramid network with auxiliary supervision, and frame-level self-distillation. Together, these mechanisms bring video features and domain-relevant information such as handshape and body movement into the recognition model, TwoStream-SLR.

Adding a translation network produces TwoStream-SLT. Experiments report state-of-the-art performance for recognition and translation across datasets including Phoenix-2014, Phoenix-2014T, and CSL-Daily. The findings support combining detailed visual observations with explicit keypoint information, while sharing information between the streams, for both identifying signs and translating sign-language video.
neurips-2022-two-stream-network-for-sign.tldr: Two interacting video and keypoint streams achieve reported state-of-the-art sign-language recognition and translation across several datasets.

paragraphs: A pretrained model may encounter a target domain whose data differ from its original training distribution. Source-free adaptation tackles this problem without access to the source data or labeled target examples. The paper proposes adapting the source model through probabilistic parameter perturbations, with the aim of retaining much of its existing ability to distinguish classes.

The perturbations are learned using variational Bayesian inference. This frames adaptation as probabilistic modification of the source model, rather than ordinary parameter fine-tuning. The authors establish a theoretical connection with Bayesian neural-network learning to support generalization to target domains. A parameter-sharing strategy reduces the number of learnable parameters substantially compared with a fully Bayesian neural network.

Experiments on several source-free adaptation benchmarks, using three evaluation settings, verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The contribution brings together target adaptation, preservation of source-model knowledge, and a more economical probabilistic parameterization. Its setting is specifically one where the original training data and labeled target data are unavailable for optimization.
neurips-2022-variational-model-perturbat.tldr: Variational parameter perturbations adapt a pretrained model without source data or labeled target examples while largely preserving its discriminative ability.

paragraphs: Human annotations of important image regions are intended to help visual question-answering models use relevant evidence. Yet prior improvements sometimes persisted with random annotations, raising doubts about meaningful alignment. VISFIS addresses this by training for four complementary behaviors: correct answers from sufficient evidence, uncertainty without important evidence, invariance to irrelevant changes, and explanations aligned with human judgments.

On benchmark datasets, the method outperforms strong baselines in both in-distribution and out-of-distribution accuracy, while improving several measures of being right for the right reason. The paper also examines why plausible explanations relate to accuracy. It finds that this relationship depends crucially on faithfulness: whether an explanation actually represents the model's internal reasoning.

Plausible and faithful explanations are associated with more accurate predictions; plausible but unfaithful explanations are not. Separately, the studied reasoning metrics do not predict out-of-distribution accuracy after controlling for in-distribution accuracy. These findings support the proposed training objectives while questioning whether those metrics, by themselves, meaningfully assess reasoning relevant to generalization.
neurips-2022-visfis-visual-feature-impor.tldr: VISFIS improves visual question answering through four evidence-focused objectives while showing that plausible explanations and reasoning metrics require careful interpretation.

paragraphs: An autonomous learning agent can reach a state it cannot recover from without outside assistance. A robot that pushes an object off a table illustrates the problem: continuing its usual interaction may not restore the task. Standard agents can therefore require ongoing monitoring so that a person can decide when to intervene.

The paper proposes an algorithm that learns to detect and avoid irreversible states, while also requesting help if it enters one. This combines prevention with recognition that recovery assistance is needed. The irreversible states are initially unknown, so the agent must learn about them as part of its interaction rather than relying on a supplied list of failure situations.

Across a suite of continuous-control environments, the algorithm achieves better sample efficiency and intervention efficiency than existing methods. The results support agents taking a more active role in managing their own need for assistance. The goal remains autonomy with help when necessary: the method addresses how to reduce and appropriately request intervention when some situations cannot be resolved by the agent alone.
neurips-2022-when-to-ask-for-help-proact.tldr: The proposed agent learns to avoid irreversible states and request recovery assistance, improving sample and intervention efficiency in continuous-control experiments.
